llm_proposer.assessment: The outage is most consistent with a hard failure of the S13 ROADM WSS input port receiving the common S23–S13 degree. It explains the simultaneous multi-channel OCH_LOS and widespread service/protection impacts while the S23–S13 line amplifiers and incoming OCM measurements remained unchanged, localizing the loss after the monitored OMS rather than in the fibre or amplifiers.

proposals.rationale: A failed S13 WSS input port on the S23-facing degree would block every arriving channel after the OMS monitors, matching the simultaneous hard OCH_LOS and common dependency. The main uncertainty is that the supplied observations do not explicitly name the failed degree or a ROADM equipment alarm.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: The corresponding WSS input port at S23 could produce a similar mass channel loss in the opposite direction while leaving line amplifier telemetry normal. It is less favored because the observed receiver losses, including at S13, fit blocking on arrival at S13 better.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A disconnected S23–S13 OMS input patch could hard-drop all channels on the common degree. However, unchanged input/output power across all amplifiers and unchanged S13 OCM power strongly argue against a break before the monitored OMS.

A cable cut could create simultaneous bidirectional service failures and hard LOS. It is very unlikely because the downstream amplifier and endpoint OCM powers on the common line reportedly showed no change; E14 is only a representative shared span, with no evidence uniquely selecting it.
